title: Spec's 'catalog_hash header re-bless is the only T1 shift' is literal-false: catalog_hash rides INSIDE every per-tick hash, so all 1500 qos.t1 lines (and every demo's) shift mechanically
evidence: spec-3-3-contention.md:29: "existing light demos' T1 stays byte-identical (catalog_hash header re-bless is the only T1 shift)"; :111: "T1 shifts ONLY when packets genuinely share a pipe (ecmp's 2-apart spawn pairs if the ECMP hash collides them; qos/qos_emphasis era-3 traffic saturates)". core/serialize.odin:88 (state_writer, FNV-1a-64'd per tick by state_hash): "w_u64(&w, state.catalog_hash)". goldens/boot.t1 tick 1: 0911fcd "1 692b13aed9005ede" -> ffc9b7b "1 47151bb2562fbe59" (single-packet demo, zero contention).
detail: Reason (a) holds (verified: harness 12/12 PASS at this sha; log.bin command streams byte-identical; boot.log.bin differs only in version+catalog hash), but the spec's letter is inaccurate: the catalog_hash VALUE is hashed into each per-tick line, so every per-tick line of every demo shifts mechanically, even with zero sim change. A 3.4/round-2 reviewer following the spec would mis-flag the light-demo per-tick shifts as unaccounted drift.
recommended_fix: Amend spec wording: the per-tick FNV-1a-64 input includes state.catalog_hash (serialize.odin:88), so the (a) catalog-key re-bless mechanically rewrites every per-tick line of every demo; sim-change-free demos are verified by unchanged command logs + the E7 lone-packet pins, not by identical per-tick lines.
